name: Christ Church Nashville — Medical Equipment Ministry
address: Christ Church Nashville, Old Hickory Blvd, Nashville, TN (call for the pickup spot)
serves: Community members who need equipment. No formal eligibility rules were reported.
loan_terms: Works like a library: keep items as long as you need them.
notes: Equipment is new or gently used and sanitized, according to the news report.

sources.title: NewsChannel 5 (WTVF): Free medical equipment 'library' helps Nashville community in need (Aug 16, 2025)

name: UCP of Middle Tennessee — Equipment Exchange
serves: People with disabilities throughout Tennessee, regardless of diagnosis — not only cerebral palsy.
cost: Free to people who can't otherwise afford the equipment
loan_terms: Equipment is placed with people who need it; ask about returns.
hours: Call to ask — a nonprofit listing says there are no set public hours.
notes: Collects, repairs and refurbishes used equipment. Volunteers sometimes deliver.

sources.title: NewsChannel 5: UCP Equipment Exchange (Ms. Cheap segment)
AARP Tennessee: Recycle Your Old Medical Equipment
Cause IQ: United Cerebral Palsy of Middle Tennessee (IRS filing data)
GivingConnection: United Cerebral Palsy of Middle TN (listing not yet verified by the nonprofit)

name: ALS Association Tennessee — Equipment Loan Closet
serves: People living with ALS who are registered with the ALS Association in Tennessee.
cost: Free loans. Limited financial help to buy needed equipment may also be available.
notes: Contact the DME Program Coordinator or your local ALS care team. To donate, fill out the program's in-kind donation form.

sources.title: ALS Association: Durable Medical Equipment Loan Closet Program (Tennessee)
GuideStar: ALS Association–Tennessee Chapter (Nashville, TN)

name: Tennessee Technology Access Program (TTAP) — Device Loan & Reuse
address: Andrew Johnson Tower, 11th Floor, 710 James Robertson Pkwy, Nashville, TN 37243
serves: People with disabilities and their families, through partner assistive technology centers in each region.
cost: Ask — loan and reuse programs are designed to widen access.
loan_terms: Device loans are short-term (try before you buy, or while you wait).
notes: TTAP's four core programs are Funding Assistance, Device Demonstration, Device Loan and Device Reutilization. Ask which regional center serves your county.

sources.title: Tennessee Department of Human Services: Tennessee Technology Access Program

name: Mid-South Access Center for Technology (University of Memphis)
address: 530 Patterson Street, 119 Patterson Hall, Memphis, TN 38152
serves: People with disabilities in Memphis and the Mid-South.
loan_terms: Short-term device loans; the reuse program passes on donated equipment.
notes: The reuse program promotes donation, repair and reuse of technology and durable medical equipment. A TTAP partner center.

sources.title: Mid-South ACT: Services
Mid-South ACT: Contact

name: STAR Center — Durable Medical Equipment
serves: West Tennessee residents who need equipment.
cost: Free (donated equipment given at no cost, per a third-party directory)
notes: One of TTAP's regional assistive technology centers. The phone number comes from a third-party directory, so confirm it before you drive over.

sources.title: SeniorsMobility: Free Medical Equipment in Tennessee (third-party list)
TTAP partner centers, including The STAR Center in Jackson (2017 presentation)

name: Spark (formerly ETTAC) — Mobility & Medical Equipment
serves: People who need mobility or medical equipment across Spark's 23-county area.
cost: A minimum donation per item is now required, but Spark says it doesn't turn people away for lack of funds.
hours: Equipment pickup: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9 a.m.–4 p.m. (per WBIR)
notes: Spark cleans and repairs donated equipment before passing it on, and has started delivery and pickup services.

sources.title: WBIR: Spark mobility expands mission
Knoxville News Sentinel (via Yahoo): Spark phone and South Knoxville office
U.S. Department of Labor directory listing: Spark formerly ETTAC (address, phone, website)

name: Goodwill of the Greater Chattanooga Area — HELPs Equipment Program
address: Goodwill Opportunity Campus, 6104 Preservation Drive, Chattanooga, TN 37416
equipment: Walkers and other durable medical equipment
serves: Anyone with a disability or injury in Goodwill's 23-county area of Southeast Tennessee and North Georgia, per AARP.
loan_terms: Goodwill asks that you return items when you no longer use them.
notes: Goodwill's HELPs program passes donated equipment on for free. AARP reported that a prescription was needed for wheelchairs and power chairs. Call to confirm the program is still running, and its current rules.

sources.title: AARP Tennessee: Recycle Your Old Medical Equipment

Warren County, TN news release listing Goodwill locations (Apr 30, 2025)

name: Signal Centers Assistive Technology Center
serves: People with disabilities in Southeast Tennessee. One of TTAP's regional assistive technology centers.
loan_terms: Ask about the TTAP device loan program.
notes: Best for assistive technology (home and workplace devices) rather than beds or wheelchairs. Ask what's available to borrow.

sources.title: Tennessee Library for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing: Signal Centers' Assistive Technology Services
TTAP partner centers (2017 presentation)

name: Roan Creek Baptist Church — Medical Equipment Ministry
address: Lumpkin Branch Road, Mountain City, TN 37683
serves: People in the community — the church reported having 'basically any item a senior adult might need.'
notes: Volunteers have picked up donated equipment and delivered to people who can't come get it, according to Baptist & Reflector. The phone number comes from church directories, so confirm it when you call.
